newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin misses G7 event, officials say "tired".
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin misses G7 event, officials say "tired".

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin missed a gala concert during the Group of Seven summit on Saturday and a White House official said he had decided not to attend because he was too tired.
A Kremlin official in Denver said: "He is in his residence, he decided that he would prefer not to take part in this event," but he added: "Tomorrow's meetings will go ahead according to plan."

Daniel Tarullo, deputy security affairs assistant to U.S. President Bill Clinton, said Yeltsin had left the summit dinner early and returned to his hotel. "He was tired, he was just tired," Tarullo told reporters.

Journalists outside a restaurant where Yeltsin attended a summit dinner before the concert said the Russian president left, apparently unexpectedly, with seven or eight aides about 20 minutes before Clinton and other leaders. Journalists had been told they would all leave together.

The concert had been included in the early schedules distributed by the Kremlin for the Russian president, and the organisers said they had expected him to join the G7 leaders from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.

Yeltsin suffered two heart attacks last year, but he had looked fit at the start of the summit. Journalists who saw him on Saturday, first full day of the gathering, said that he looked tired and moved stiffly.
